name: Heliodorus
description: Treasurer to king Seleucus, sent to Jerusalem to seize the temple treasury on the report of Simon and Apollonius; struck down and scourged by a horseman and two young men from heaven when he entered the treasury with his guard, and healed after Onias the high priest offered sacrifice for him; he then testified to the king of the mighty power of God at that place

points: Apollonius told the king of the money, and the king chose Heliodorus his treasurer and sent him to bring the money. Heliodorus took his journey under a colour of visiting the cities of Coelosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king's purpose: that is what he let everybody think he was doing.

Heliodorus's friends begged Onias to call upon the Most High to grant him his life. The high priest, suspecting lest the king should think some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the health of the man. The same young men appeared and said, give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake the Lord hath granted thee life; and seeing that thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God.

This Simon, having been a bewrayer of the money and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus and been the worker of these evils. He told the Greeks that Onias did that to Heliodorus. Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws. He called that type of a brother a traitor.

cases.name: Heliodorus
cases.charge: Attempting to plunder the temple treasury
cases.preview: While Onias was high priest the holy city was inhabited with all peace and the laws were kept very well, so that even the heathen kings honoured the temple.
